speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to speak about Bill 23, An Act to Amend the Legislative Assembly Act, a critical piece of legislation that will help safeguard the integrity of our esteemed Legislative Assembly. This bill is not just a step towards transparency and accountability; it is a leap. It underscores our commitment to the people of New Brunswick, demonstrating our unwavering dedication to the principles of honesty, fairness, and good governance.

Bill 23 aims to strengthen the code of conduct for members, enhance the conflict of interest rules, and improve the management of external interests. These measures will ensure that the actions of each member are guided by the highest ethical standards.

In a democratic society, the trust of the people is paramount. By passing this bill, we will bolster that trust, showing that we are not just politicians, but public servants dedicated to the well-being of our province and its citizens. I urge all members to support Bill 23, because integrity matters, and our Legislative Assembly deserves nothing less.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The government's Bill 23, the Elections Modernization and Other Matters Act, is a direct assault on the integrity of our Legislative Assembly. The bill, in its current form, threatens transparency by weakening the powers of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner. This undermines public trust in our democratic institutions, and I call upon the government to reconsider these provisions.

Will the government commit to upholding the integrity of our Legislative Assembly by amending Bill 23 to protect the independence of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner? Furthermore, will the government agree to a comprehensive review of all measures that could potentially undermine the transparency and accountability of our elected representatives?

Let us remember that our duty is to serve the people of New Brunswick, not to erode the trust they have placed in us.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with great pride and a profound sense of responsibility to address this Honorable Assembly. I am honored to present an update on Bill 23, An Act to amend the Legislative Assembly Act, which aims to further strengthen the integrity of our cherished institution, the Legislative Assembly of New Brunswick.

I am pleased to report that significant progress has been made in the development of this crucial legislation. After extensive consultations with various stakeholders and a thorough review of best practices from across Canada, we have refined the bill to ensure it addresses the core issues of transparency, accountability, and ethical conduct.

The proposed amendments will modernize the rules governing the Legislative Assembly, enhancing public trust and confidence in our democratic process. Key elements include strengthened conflict of interest provisions, improved lobbyist regulations, and increased transparency in the reporting of gifts and expenses.

We remain committed to fostering a culture of integrity within our legislature, where the highest ethical standards are upheld. I am confident that the passage of Bill 23 will reaffirm New Brunswickers' faith in their elected representatives and their belief in the vital role the Legislative Assembly plays in our democracy.

I look forward to continuing our collaborative efforts in this important endeavor, working together to ensure a legislature that serves the best interests of all New Brunswickers. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the concerns raised by the opposition regarding Bill 23 and the integrity of our Legislative Assembly. Our government is committed to ensuring transparency, accountability, and the highest ethical standards. Bill 23 is a necessary step to modernize our governance and strengthen the accountability of our elected officials.

The opposition's mischaracterizations are misleading and unfounded. This bill is not a power grab, but an essential measure to protect our democracy and ensure public trust. It is designed to clarify the roles and responsibilities of the Speaker, improve the code of conduct, and strengthen oversight mechanisms.

We have consulted extensively with all parties, stakeholders, and experts, and we have taken their feedback into account in drafting this bill. We will continue to work collaboratively to ensure the best possible outcome for all New Brunswickers.

Madam Speaker, our government is committed to working in the best interests of the people of New Brunswick. We stand by Bill 23 and its intentions to strengthen our democratic institutions and enhance the integrity of our Legislative Assembly.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to discuss the proposed capital budget for the fiscal year 2026-27, totaling $1.47 billion. This budget reflects our government's commitment to investing in the future of New Brunswick, ensuring economic growth, and improving the lives of our citizens.

The budget allocates significant funds towards infrastructure projects, including the modernization of our schools, hospitals, and highways. These investments will not only create jobs but also enhance the quality of life for our residents.

In education, we have earmarked funds for the construction of new schools and the renovation of existing ones, ensuring our students learn in safe, modern, and conducive environments. In healthcare, we are investing in the expansion of our hospitals, improving access to quality care for all New Brunswickers.

In addition, we have allocated resources for the maintenance and improvement of our roads and bridges, addressing the needs of our growing population and supporting economic growth.

This budget is a testament to our government's dedication to building a stronger, more prosperous New Brunswick. I urge my colleagues to support this budget, as it lays the foundation for a brighter future for our province.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with concerns regarding the government's 2026-27 capital budget of $1.47 billion. Despite our province's ongoing economic struggles, the government has allocated an unprecedented amount to capital projects. Can the government assure this House that this investment will be prudent, transparent, and focused on projects that will drive economic growth and create jobs for New Brunswickers?

Moreover, will the government commit to a comprehensive review of its capital spending priorities, ensuring that every dollar spent will benefit our province and not just the pockets of well-connected insiders? The people of New Brunswick deserve to know that their tax dollars are being spent wisely.

Let's prioritize our future, Madam Speaker. Let's invest in New Brunswickers.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to present an overview of the 2026-27 capital budget, a strategic investment plan that reflects our government's commitment to building a stronger and more resilient New Brunswick. With a total allocation of $1.47 billion, this budget is a testament to our promise of a better future for all our citizens.

The budget is meticulously designed to address key areas of focus, including infrastructure, education, health, and economic development. Significant investments have been made to modernize schools, hospitals, and public buildings, ensuring they meet the needs of our growing and diverse population.

Investments in transportation infrastructure will enhance our connectivity, fostering economic growth and mobility across our province. Our focus on education includes the construction of new schools and the renovation of existing facilities, aimed at providing our students with a conducive learning environment.

In the realm of health, we have allocated resources to modernize hospitals, expand mental health services, and improve long-term care facilities, prioritizing the well-being of our citizens. To support our economic development, we have earmarked funds for strategic infrastructure projects, fostering job creation and attracting investment.

This budget is a testament to our government's commitment to building a better future for New Brunswick. I am confident that these investments will yield long-term benefits for our province, and I look forward to working with all members of this legislative assembly to see these projects through.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker, I rise today to address the opposition's concerns regarding the 2026-27 capital budget of $1.47 billion. This budget is a strategic investment in our province's future, not an extravagant expenditure.

Our government has carefully planned this budget to prioritize infrastructure projects that will stimulate economic growth, create jobs, and improve the quality of life for all New Brunswickers. The proposed investments in education, healthcare, and transportation are long-term commitments to our province's prosperity.

We understand the importance of fiscal responsibility and have ensured that this budget is balanced and sustainable. The projects included have been meticulously evaluated based on their potential to drive economic growth and social development.

The opposition's criticism is misguided. This budget is an investment in our province's future, not a financial burden. We are committed to building a stronger, more prosperous New Brunswick for all its citizens.

I urge the opposition to join us in supporting this strategic and necessary investment in our province's future. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to commend our government on the innovative Nursing Home Without Walls program, a groundbreaking initiative that enhances the quality of life for our seniors. This program enables elderly individuals to live independently in their homes while still receiving critical healthcare services. By bridging the gap between home and nursing home care, we are not only improving the health outcomes for our seniors but also fostering a sense of independence and dignity.

The Nursing Home Without Walls program represents a significant step forward in our province's commitment to aging with grace and dignity. It empowers our seniors to maintain their autonomy while providing them with the support they need. This approach is not only compassionate, but it is also cost-effective and sustainable, ensuring that our resources are used in a way that benefits both our seniors and the province as a whole.

I urge my colleagues to support this forward-thinking initiative. Let us continue to strive for a New Brunswick where our seniors can age with dignity, independence, and the support they deserve. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The government's Nursing Home Without Walls program was hailed as a groundbreaking initiative to support our seniors, allowing them to age in place with dignity and independence. However, a growing number of concerned families have reported significant delays and inadequate support in accessing this program. Can the Minister of Health provide the House with an update on the current state of the Nursing Home Without Walls program, including the reasons for these delays, the number of seniors still awaiting support, and the government's plan to ensure timely and effective implementation of this essential service?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with a profound sense of fulfillment to update the Honourable Members on the significant advancements in our government's commitment to the well-being of our senior citizens through the Nursing Home Without Walls program.

This innovative initiative, a testament to our government's forward-thinking approach, has made considerable strides, enabling more seniors to age with dignity and independence in their homes. The program, launched in earnest last year, has already served over 500 seniors, providing them with access to essential healthcare services, mental health support, and social connections, all from the comfort of their homes.

The success of this program is a collective effort, a symphony of collaboration between our dedicated healthcare professionals, community partners, and, most importantly, our resilient seniors. We are indeed grateful for their trust and cooperation.

As we move forward, we remain committed to expanding the program's reach, ensuring that no senior in New Brunswick feels isolated or overlooked. Our vision is to make New Brunswick a beacon of aged care excellence, where seniors can thrive in their golden years, surrounded by the care, respect, and dignity they deserve.

I invite all Honourable Members to join us in celebrating this progress and to continue supporting our seniors in their journey towards a fulfilling and independent life. Together, we are building a brighter future for New Brunswick's seniors.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the concerns raised by the opposition about the Nursing Home Without Walls program. This innovative program is a testament to our government's commitment to enhancing the quality of life for our senior citizens. It offers seniors the opportunity to live independently in their homes, while still receiving necessary healthcare services.

The program's success is evident in the improved quality of care, increased autonomy for seniors, and cost savings for our healthcare system. It's not just a program; it's a symbol of our commitment to respecting the dignity and independence of our elderly population.

To the opposition, I say this: We understand the importance of caring for our seniors, and this program is one of many ways we are doing just that. We will continue to strive for excellence in our healthcare services, and we invite the opposition to join us in this noble pursuit.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

Today, I stand before this honorable House to address a pressing issue that impacts our society deeply - addiction treatment and mental health services in New Brunswick. Our province is home to resilient individuals and families, yet many are struggling in silence, battling the stigma and challenges associated with mental health issues and addiction.

We must acknowledge the vital role of early intervention, prevention, and support for those in need. I urge my fellow Members to recognize that investing in mental health and addiction services is not just a humanitarian responsibility, but an economic imperative. A healthy population contributes to a vibrant and prosperous province.

I propose we work collaboratively to enhance our current services, ensuring they are accessible, equitable, and evidence-based. This includes increased funding for community-based programs, expanding the availability of telehealth services, and advocating for the destigmatization of mental health issues.

Let us demonstrate our commitment to the well-being of our people by prioritizing mental health and addiction treatment. Together, we can build a brighter future for New Brunswick, one where every individual has access to the care they need to live a healthy, fulfilling life.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The people of New Brunswick deserve access to timely, effective mental health and addiction services. The government's current strategy has failed to address the growing crisis, with long waitlists and inadequate resources. Can the Minister of Health explain why, despite the escalating need, the government has not increased funding for mental health and addiction services in the recent budget? What specific measures will the government take to ensure our citizens have the help they need to overcome these debilitating illnesses?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to update the Honourable Members on our government's unwavering commitment to addressing addiction and mental health challenges in our province.

I am delighted to announce significant progress in our efforts to expand and enhance treatment and support services for those affected by these complex issues. Our government has invested $10 million in the development of a new Mental Health and Addiction Centre of Excellence. This centre will serve as a hub for research, education, and clinical care, fostering a collaborative approach to addressing these issues.

In addition, we have increased funding for community-based addiction treatment programs by 40%, ensuring more individuals have access to the help they need, when they need it. We are also expanding the capacity of our residential treatment facilities, providing a safe and supportive environment for recovery.

We acknowledge the urgency of these issues and are committed to continuous improvement. A Mental Health and Addictions Action Plan will be unveiled in the coming weeks, outlining our comprehensive strategy for addressing these challenges.

Our government is dedicated to creating a New Brunswick where every resident has the opportunity to live a healthy, fulfilling life. This is just the beginning of our journey. Together, we will make a difference.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the concerns raised by the opposition regarding addiction treatment and mental health services in our province. Our government acknowledges the urgency of this matter and is committed to ensuring our citizens receive the care they deserve.

We have taken significant steps to expand and improve mental health and addiction services. The establishment of the Mental Health and Addictions Action Plan, the $10 million investment in the Capital Health Mental Health and Addiction Strategy, and the creation of the Rapid Access Addiction Medicine clinics are testament to our commitment.

However, we understand that more needs to be done. That's why we are working closely with health professionals, community organizations, and the public to further enhance our services. Our government will continue to invest in evidence-based strategies to address the challenges posed by addiction and mental health issues.

We are not resting on our laurels, Madam Speaker. We are committed to building a healthier New Brunswick, one that provides the support our citizens need when they need it most. We are here for them, and we will continue to work tirelessly to improve mental health and addiction services in our province.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to discuss a matter of pressing concern for our constituents: property assessment freezes and new fees. As we navigate these challenging economic times, it is essential that we provide relief where possible. I am advocating for a temporary property assessment freeze for New Brunswickers. Homeowners have been hit hard by inflation and rising costs, and a freeze on property assessments would offer some much-needed respite.

However, I also recognize that our province needs sustainable revenue streams. To balance this, I propose the introduction of new, targeted fees for specific services. For instance, a small fee for online services could help offset the costs of maintaining these platforms, while a fee for luxury items like boats and RVs could generate revenue without unduly burdening the majority.

By implementing a thoughtful combination of a property assessment freeze and targeted fees, we can support New Brunswickers and secure our province's financial future. I urge my colleagues to join me in advocating for this balanced approach.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The government's recent announcement of a property assessment freeze, accompanied by new fees for essential services, raises serious concerns. While we understand the need for fiscal prudence, the combination of these measures will disproportionately burden middle-class families, small businesses, and those on fixed incomes. The government's rationale for these measures is unclear, and we call on the government to provide a detailed explanation of how these changes will stimulate economic growth, support our communities, and protect the most vulnerable residents during these challenging times. Will the government commit to a thorough and transparent analysis of the potential impacts of these policies before implementation?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with a significant update on our government's commitment to homeowners across New Brunswick. I am pleased to announce that we have made significant progress on the property assessment freeze and the introduction of new fees, as part of our ongoing efforts to provide relief and promote fairness in our property tax system.

Following extensive consultations with municipalities, homeowners, and stakeholders, I am proud to inform the House that we will be implementing a two-year property assessment freeze, effective January 1, 2023. This measure will help stabilize property taxes for homeowners, offering much-needed respite in these challenging economic times.

Simultaneously, we are introducing a new system of fairer, more transparent fees for property assessments. These fees will be based on the size and complexity of the property, ensuring a more equitable distribution of the cost across all property owners.

We believe these measures will not only provide relief to homeowners but also foster a more efficient and sustainable property tax system for New Brunswick. Our government remains committed to listening to the concerns of our citizens and working tirelessly to build a stronger, more prosperous province for all.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the concerns raised by the opposition regarding our government's property assessment freeze and new fees. The property assessment freeze is a significant step towards providing relief to our hardworking New Brunswickers. This measure, combined with our ongoing efforts to reduce property taxes, demonstrates our commitment to alleviating the financial burden on homeowners.

Regarding the new fees, it's essential to understand that they are strategically designed to fund critical services such as road maintenance, infrastructure improvements, and the enhancement of public spaces. These investments are crucial for our province's long-term economic growth and the overall well-being of our communities.

Our government is committed to transparency and fairness. We have taken steps to ensure that the new fees are reasonable and equitably distributed. We have also provided exemptions for vulnerable populations, such as low-income households and seniors, to ensure no one is unduly burdened.

In conclusion, Madam Speaker, our government is working diligently to strike a balance between fiscal responsibility and the well-being of New Brunswickers. We will continue to listen to the concerns of all members in this Assembly and make adjustments as necessary to ensure a brighter future for our province. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address a pressing concern that affects the safety, well-being, and educational opportunities of our young people – school bus breakdowns and student transportation issues.

The recent spike in incidents has left many students stranded, parents anxious, and schools scrambling to ensure children reach their destinations safely. This is unacceptable and demands immediate attention.

I call upon the government to invest in modernizing our school bus fleet, ensuring they are equipped with reliable technology to reduce breakdowns and improve safety. Furthermore, we must enhance maintenance schedules and training for drivers to minimize these incidents.

We must remember that every student deserves a safe and timely journey to school. Let us work together, Madam Speaker, to prioritize our children's safety and provide them with the best possible start to their day – in school, on time, and ready to learn.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The government's failure to ensure reliable student transportation is causing undue stress for families and putting our students' safety at risk. Over the past year, there have been numerous reports of school bus breakdowns and delays, leaving students stranded. The Department of Education has stated that they are working to address these issues, but action is long overdue.

I ask the Minister responsible, what steps is the government taking to rectify this situation? How can we be sure that our children will be safely transported to and from school every day? When will the government prioritize student safety and ensure that our school bus system is reliable and effective?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I stand before this esteemed house to address a matter of significant importance to our province's future: the efficient and safe transportation of our students to and from school. I am pleased to report substantial progress in our ongoing efforts to address school bus breakdowns and improve student transportation services in New Brunswick.

Our government has been working diligently with key stakeholders to implement innovative solutions aimed at enhancing reliability and reducing the frequency of school bus breakdowns. This includes investing in preventative maintenance programs, upgrading aging fleets, and improving training and support for our dedicated school bus drivers.

Furthermore, we have initiated a comprehensive review of the school transportation system to identify areas for improvement and streamline operations. This includes the introduction of a centralized dispatch system, which will improve communication and response times in the event of unexpected issues.

We understand the critical role that safe and reliable transportation plays in our children's lives and in their academic success. Our government is committed to ensuring that every student in New Brunswick has access to a safe, reliable, and efficient school transportation service.

I would like to express my gratitude to the hardworking individuals who make this vital service possible, and to the parents and students who have patiently endured challenges in the past. I am confident that these initiatives will lead to a brighter future for student transportation in our province.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the concerns raised by members of the opposition regarding school bus breakdowns and student transportation. While it is unfortunate that incidents have occurred, I assure this Assembly that our government is deeply committed to the safety and well-being of our students.

To address this issue, we have increased our investment in school bus maintenance, ensuring that our fleet is well-maintained and up-to-date. We have also implemented a comprehensive training program for bus drivers to enhance their skills and knowledge.

Furthermore, we have established a hotline for parents and students to report any issues or concerns about school bus services. This hotline is monitored 24/7 to ensure prompt action is taken.

We understand the importance of a reliable school transportation system and are taking every measure to improve it. However, I urge the opposition to constructively engage with us in finding solutions, rather than simply criticizing without offering alternatives.

Let us work together to ensure the best possible education environment for our children. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the critical matter of the Mactaquac dam refurbishment and the debt burden on New Brunswick Hydro, now known as NB Power.

The Mactaquac dam is a vital part of our province's energy infrastructure, but it is in desperate need of modernization. The refurbishment project, estimated at over $4 billion, is a significant investment, but one that is necessary to ensure the continued, reliable supply of electricity for our province.

However, this investment comes at a time when NB Power is already burdened with a heavy debt load. The question before us is not whether we invest in the Mactaquac dam refurbishment, but how we do so in a manner that is fiscally responsible and sustainable.

I call on the government to work with NB Power, stakeholders, and the public to develop a comprehensive plan for the refurbishment that prioritizes affordability for ratepayers, protects our environment, and secures our energy future.

Let us work together to ensure that the Mactaquac dam refurbishment is not just a cost, but an investment in our province's future prosperity. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

The people of New Brunswick are concerned about the ballooning debt and the future of Mactaquac Dam. The refurbishment project has been plagued with delays, cost overruns, and questionable decisions, all while NB Power's debt continues to climb.

Will the government clearly outline what steps it intends to take to ensure transparency and accountability in the Mactaquac dam refurbishment project, and what measures are being taken to address NB Power's mounting debt, which currently stands at over $6 billion?

The people of New Brunswick deserve answers and a plan for a more financially stable and sustainable future for our province.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with great pride and optimism to address the House on the significant strides made in the Mactaquac Dam refurbishment project and the ongoing efforts to address the debt of NB Power.

The Mactaquac Dam refurbishment, a project of national significance, is progressing steadily. The design phase is nearing completion, and the procurement process for the main civil works contract is underway. This refurbishment will extend the life of the dam by 50 years, ensuring a reliable and sustainable energy source for New Brunswickers.

In terms of NB Power's debt, we have made substantial progress. Our government has successfully refinanced $1.7 billion of NB Power's debt, lowering annual interest payments and freeing up funds for vital infrastructure projects. We are committed to reducing the debt and securing a financially sustainable future for NB Power.

Our government is working tirelessly to ensure the economic prosperity and energy security of New Brunswick. The Mactaquac Dam refurbishment and our debt management strategy are crucial steps in this journey. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the people of New Brunswick, ensuring a brighter, more sustainable future for all.

Madam Speaker, I assure this House and the people of New Brunswick that we will continue to work diligently to deliver on our promises. Together, we are building a stronger, more resilient province for future generations.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the opposition's unfounded criticism regarding the Mactaquac dam refurbishment and NB Power's debt. Our government has always prioritized the long-term sustainability and growth of our province, and the Mactaquac dam refurbishment is a crucial part of this vision.

The decision to refurbish the dam was not made lightly. It was based on extensive research, engineering studies, and expert advice, all of which confirmed that refurbishment is the most cost-effective and environmentally responsible option. The project will ensure a reliable source of clean, renewable energy for our province and create jobs during construction and beyond.

Regarding NB Power's debt, it is important to note that the utility operates in a highly regulated environment and faces significant costs, including the need to modernize and maintain our aging infrastructure. Our government is committed to working with NB Power to find solutions that are in the best interest of all New Brunswickers, including ratepayers.

In conclusion, Madam Speaker, our government remains focused on building a strong and sustainable future for New Brunswick, and the Mactaquac dam refurbishment is an essential part of this vision. We will continue to make evidence-based decisions that benefit our province and its people.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today with deep gratitude in my heart to acknowledge the unsung heroes who bravely stood against the fierce and formidable foe that was last summer's wildfire. Our firefighters, both professional and volunteer, put their lives on the line to protect our homes, our communities, and our precious natural resources.

In the face of intense heat, smoke, and uncertainty, they demonstrated courage, resilience, and a selflessness that is truly humbling. Their tireless efforts, often working in challenging and dangerous conditions, have left an indelible mark on the hearts of all New Brunswickers.

These brave men and women, our firefighters, are the embodiment of our province's spirit - strong, compassionate, and unwavering in the face of adversity. I stand here today to express our collective gratitude, and to remind them that their sacrifice will never be forgotten.

To every firefighter who served, I say thank you. Your bravery and dedication have made a profound impact on our province, and we are eternally grateful for your service. Let us continue to support them in their crucial work, ensuring they have the resources and recognition they deserve.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to commend our brave firefighters who tirelessly fought the devastating wildfires that ravaged our province last summer. These heroes put their lives on the line to protect our homes, our communities, and our precious natural resources.

While we are grateful for their efforts, I cannot help but question the government's lack of acknowledgement and support for these selfless individuals. I ask the Minister responsible, when will our government formally thank our firefighters for their unwavering dedication, and what measures are being taken to ensure they receive the compensation and resources they need to continue serving our province?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

Today, I rise in this Honourable Assembly to express our collective gratitude to the brave firefighters who tirelessly served our province during last summer's wildfires. Their dedication, courage, and selflessness were unwavering, and their efforts saved countless lives and properties.

Our government recognizes the significant role these heroes played in protecting our communities and ensuring the safety of our citizens. We are committed to expressing our appreciation in a meaningful and lasting way.

I am pleased to announce that we have taken initial steps towards establishing a Firefighter Recognition Program. This program will acknowledge the extraordinary work of our firefighters and provide them with the respect and appreciation they deserve.

Furthermore, we are in discussions with various organizations to create a memorial that will serve as a lasting testament to the bravery and sacrifice of our firefighters. This memorial will stand as a symbol of our gratitude and a reminder of the courage displayed during those challenging times.

Our firefighters are true heroes, and it is our responsibility to ensure they know they are valued and appreciated. We will continue to work diligently to honour their service and create a program that reflects the depth of our appreciation.

Madam Speaker, we stand with our firefighters today, tomorrow, and always. Their dedication to our province is a beacon of hope and resilience that we will never forget.

Thank you.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker, I rise today to address the unfounded criticism levied against this government for expressing our deepest gratitude to our brave firefighters who valiantly battled last summer's devastating wildfires. It is not only our duty but our privilege to acknowledge and honor their exceptional service. These heroes put their lives on the line, risking everything to protect our communities and homes.

To suggest that we should not recognize their efforts is not only disheartening but shows a profound disregard for the sacrifices they made. Our firefighters are the epitome of bravery, selflessness, and dedication. They are the backbone of our emergency services, and their contribution to our province cannot be understated.

We will continue to stand with our firefighters, to support them, and to ensure they have the resources they need to serve our communities effectively. Let us remember that we are all united in our admiration and gratitude for our firefighters. They are the unsung heroes of our province, and they deserve our endless praise and support. Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to acknowledge and celebrate the vibrant Diwali festivities taking place across our diverse New Brunswick communities. Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is a sacred occasion for millions of people around the world, including many of our fellow New Brunswickers.

This five-day Hindu festival symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. It is a time for family, friends, and community to come together, share meals, exchange gifts, and light the Diya, symbolizing the triumph of righteousness and the lifting of spiritual darkness.

In our multicultural province, Diwali celebrations have become a cherished tradition, showcasing the rich cultural tapestry that makes New Brunswick such a wonderful place to live. I encourage all members to join in the spirit of Diwali, learning from the values it embodies, and reinforcing our commitment to unity, respect, and understanding.

On behalf of my constituents and all New Brunswickers, I extend warm greetings to those celebrating Diwali this year. May the light of Diwali fill your homes with joy, your hearts with peace, and your lives with prosperity.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to address the lack of government recognition for Diwali, a significant festival for millions of New Brunswickers. While we celebrate Christmas and other religious holidays with official events, Diwali, the festival of lights, is often overlooked. I call on this government to acknowledge the diversity of our province and to show respect to all our communities by officially recognizing Diwali and supporting its celebrations. Will the Minister responsible for multiculturalism commit to making Diwali an official holiday in New Brunswick?

speaker: SYNTHETIC
text:
Madam Speaker,

I rise today to share significant advancements in our ongoing efforts to celebrate the rich cultural diversity of New Brunswick. I am proud to announce that preparations for the Diwali celebrations are progressing steadily, with increased participation from various communities across our province.

This year, we are delighted to welcome several new partners, including the Indian Merchants' Association of Moncton and the South Asian Association of Greater Saint John, who will contribute to making this event a memorable occasion for all.

In alignment with our commitment to fostering unity, understanding, and mutual respect among our citizens, we have secured funding to support these events, ensuring a grand display of the vibrant Diwali traditions. We are particularly excited about the collaborative efforts to organize a series of workshops, showcasing Indian art, music, and cuisine.

We believe that these celebrations will not only enrich our cultural landscape but also strengthen the bonds of friendship and cooperation among our diverse communities. I urge all New Brunswickers to join us in celebrating this festival of lights and unity.

Together, we are creating a more inclusive, vibrant, and harmonious New Brunswick for all.

Thank you, Madam Speaker.

As we celebrate National Police Week, let us renew our commitment to supporting our police force and embracing community policing. For it is through these efforts that we can build stronger, safer communities together.
